senses.gloss:
ऋच् + -तन्त्रम्, -व्याकरणम्,
[]
 N. of the Pariśiṣtas of the Sāma Veda.

ऋच् + -विधानम् the performance of certain rites, by reciting verses
 of the Ṛgveda.

ऋच् + -वेदः the oldest of the four Vedas, and the most ancient sacred
 book of the Hindus. [The Ṛgveda is said to have been produced from fire;
 cf. Ms. 1. 23. This Veda is divided, according to one arrangement, into 8
 Aṣṭakas, each of which is divided into as many Adhyāyas; according
 to another arrangement into 10 Maṇḍalas, which are again subdivided
 into 1000 Anuvākas, and comprises 1000 sūktas. The total number of verses
 or Ṛks is above 10000].
